---
name: brand-voice
description: Apply [Business] voice and tone to any user-facing copy, microcopy or marketing text, in English and Greek.
---
Save this file as .claude/skills/brand-voice/SKILL.md. Replace every bracket.
Lead with examples, not adjectives: paste three short samples of the real
voice under "Examples" and the model will learn more from them than from
any description.

Audience: [who reads this brand's words, in one sentence].

Voice: [three or four words — warm, precise, confident — and one sentence on
what the brand never sounds like]. Reading level: [plain English, B1–B2].

Tone by context:
- Success: brief and warm. Name what happened.
- Error: calm. Say what went wrong and the next step. Never blame, never apologise.
- Empty state: invite one action.
- Loading: neutral; say what is loading.
- Marketing: [confident / understated / playful]; claims only with proof.
- Support: patient; one idea per sentence.
- If the person is clearly frustrated: extra reassuring, shorter sentences.

Terminology:
- Say "[term]", not "[term]".
- Say "[term]", not "[term]".
- Never use: [list].

Hard rules:
- Sentence case for headings and buttons.
- Buttons say the action ("Save changes"), never "Submit" or "OK".
- An action keeps its name through the flow: "Publish" → "Published".
- No exclamation marks in errors. [Exclamation marks elsewhere: yes/no.]
- Length limits: see content/microcopy-matrix.md.

Greek:
- Formality: [εσείς / εσύ] and why.
- Use content/glossary-el.md for every product term.
- Flag any line where idiom or tone will not carry; offer a transcreation.
- Mark every Greek line "awaiting native review" until a native reviewer signs it off.

Examples of the voice (real, approved):
1. [paste]
2. [paste]
3. [paste]

Before returning copy: check it against every rule above and the length of
the element it goes in. Return three options with a one-line rationale each
unless asked for one.
